summary: Register 1C as the first ERP reference provider using a configured read-only standard OData baseline, exact inventory quantities and existing Task-010/013/014 mapping and reconciliation primitives without adding 1C identifiers to Core.

impacts.evidence: 1C publication/mapping configuration resolves only from the validated host-owned connector account; organization/workspace remain host-owned and provider code has no tenant persistence authority.
Committed OData fixtures are synthetic; credentials remain scoped secret bytes and remote bodies/raw transport errors are not stored as evidence.
Task 015 adds no public TORGNEXA HTTP endpoint or OpenAPI operation.
The provider is read-only and introduces no EventBus schema; Task 013 owns propagation metadata.

Frozen Connector/Runtime roots remain unchanged. Task 015 adds only additive ERP capability-specific read projections/interfaces for already-declared erp.catalog.read and erp.inventory.read capabilities.
Task 015 adds no migration; connector accounts, entity mappings, sync state and reconciliation evidence already exist.

Provider code has no direct network/database/filesystem/process/Core/App authority. TLS transport and egress are host-mediated; Basic credentials exist only inside SecretAccessor callbacks; configuration rejects traversal/query/control characters.
Manifest is strictly read-only and grants neither erp.catalog.write nor erp.orders.write; no remote mutation or destructive local action is introduced.
Remote reads do not mutate business state. Any later sync apply retains existing Task-003/030 obligations.

1C Ref_Key remains a remote mapping key, DataVersion remains opaque remote revision evidence, archive is explicit, cursors are mapping-fingerprint-bound, and Task-014 performs scheduled-full/on-demand drift control.
1C transport is host-injected and actual TLS/DNS policy remains Task-029 authority; provider code imports no net package.
Metadata/auth/rate/service outcomes normalize to bounded SDK health/error states; production SLO thresholds remain Task 066.
Suspend the connector account or remove the 1C provider route to stop reads; no database rollback is required.
Deterministic OData fixtures cover configured mapping, archive/revision, exact balances, cursor binding and adversarial response cases; the Task-064 machine report passes all thirteen checks.
